source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: Past the taped Departures gate, along the winding queue. Each traveller with barely three trays surrenders belongings onto the belt, past the scanner, right beneath the archway, its detector, wherever they walk, because they have been signaled, the guard beside the barrier toward them. Instructions blare out. A bag of contraband is flagged among four beside the officers scrutinizing coldly at it. She wands him while patting the shoulders a hand explores thoroughly. The impersonal courtesy which is performed feels almost gentle. Calmly she steps, a stray passenger, and I wave her forward against him. One moment later I greet her through the Central Terminal Two beside security within the Green Concourse Four. It is beyond a threshold he must clear where she must produce the necessary papers stamped by her agency. She hands them back, quietly past the desk and again.
